Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a classification for products, helping to organize the catalog.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

name.description: The name of the category (e.g., 'ESP Devices', 'Arduino Projects').

description.description: A brief description of what the category entails.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a product available for purchase in the MicroChub store.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

description.description: A detailed description of the product.

technicalSpecs.description: An array of key-value pairs representing technical specifications of the product.

images.description: An array of URLs to images showcasing the product.

price.description: The base price of the product.

stockQuantity.description: The current number of units of this product available in stock.

categoryId.description: Reference to the Category this product belongs to. (Relationship: Category 1:N Product)

useCases.description: An array of descriptive use cases or applications for the product.

isConfigurable.description: Indicates if this product offers customization options.

configurationOptionIds.description: References to ProductConfigurationOption entities available for this product if 'isConfigurable' is true. (Relationship: Product N:N ProductConfigurationOption)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the product was added to the catalog.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the product's information was last updated.

ProductConfigurationOption.title: ProductConfigurationOption
ProductConfigurationOption.description: Defines a type of customization available for a configurable product.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ProductConfigurationOption entity.

name.description: The name of the configuration option (e.g., 'Hardware Configuration', 'Case/Enclosure').

description.description: A brief explanation of this configuration option.

productId.description: Reference to the Product this configuration option belongs to. (Relationship: Product 1:N ProductConfigurationOption)

required.description: Indicates if selecting a value for this option is mandatory for the product.

ProductConfigurationValue.title: ProductConfigurationValue
ProductConfigurationValue.description: Represents a specific choice or value for a ProductConfigurationOption.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ProductConfigurationValue entity.

optionId.description: Reference to the ProductConfigurationOption this value belongs to. (Relationship: ProductConfigurationOption 1:N ProductConfigurationValue)

name.description: The display name of the configuration value (e.g., 'ESP32 S3', 'Acrylic Case').

priceAdjustment.description: The monetary adjustment to the product's base price when this value is selected (can be positive, negative, or zero).

description.description: An optional detailed description of this configuration value.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a registered user of the MicroChub application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity (typically from an external authentication system like Firebase).

email.description: The user's email address, used for communication and identification.

displayName.description: The public display name chosen by the user.

phoneNumber.description: The user's phone number, for order-related communications (optional).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user's profile information was last updated.

Address.title: Address
Address.description: Represents a physical address associated with a user, typically for shipping.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Address entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this address. (Relationship: User 1:N Address)

addressLine2.description: Optional secondary address line (e.g., apartment, suite, building).

stateProvince.description: The state or province of the address (e.g., Governorate in Egypt, optional).

postalCode.description: The postal code of the address (optional).

isDefault.description: Indicates if this is the user's default shipping address.

recipientName.description: The name of the person expected to receive the package at this address.

recipientPhoneNumber.description: The phone number for the recipient at this address, for delivery coordination.

WishlistItem.title: WishlistItem
WishlistItem.description: Represents a product that a user has added to their wishlist.

id.description: Unique identifier for the WishlistItem entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this wishlist item. (Relationship: User 1:N WishlistItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product in the wishlist. (Relationship: Product 1:N WishlistItem)

addedAt.description: Timestamp when the product was added to the wishlist.

Cart.title: Cart
Cart.description: Represents a user's shopping cart, holding items they intend to purchase.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Cart entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this cart. (Relationship: User 1:1 Cart)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the cart was initially created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the cart was last modified.

CartItem.title: CartItem
CartItem.description: Represents a single product within a user's shopping cart, including quantity and selected configurations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CartItem entity.

cartId.description: Reference to the Cart this item belongs to. (Relationship: Cart 1:N CartItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product in the cart. (Relationship: Product 1:N CartItem)

quantity.description: The quantity of the product in the cart (minimum 1).

selectedConfigurationValueIds.description: References to the specific ProductConfigurationValue entities chosen for this product instance in the cart. (Relationship: ProductConfigurationValue N:N CartItem)

Order.title: Order
Order.description: Represents a customer's placed order, containing details about payment, shipping, and status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Order entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who placed the order. (Relationship: User 1:N Order)

orderDate.description: Timestamp when the order was placed.

totalAmount.description: The total monetary value of the order.

status.description: The current status of the order (e.g., 'Pending', 'Confirmed', 'Processing', 'Ready', 'Completed', 'Cancelled').

paymentMethod.description: The payment method chosen by the user (e.g., 'Instapay', 'Telda').

paymentProofImageUrl.description: URL to the screenshot uploaded by the user as proof of payment.

isDepositPayment.description: Indicates if the payment made was a deposit or the full amount.

remainingAmountDue.description: The remaining balance due if 'isDepositPayment' is true, otherwise 0.

shippingAddressId.description: Reference to the Address entity used for shipping this order. (Relationship: Address 1:N Order)

trackingNumber.description: The tracking number for the shipment (optional).

paymentVerificationDate.description: Timestamp when an admin manually verified the payment proof.

lastStatusUpdateDate.description: Timestamp when the order status was last updated.

OrderItem.title: OrderItem
OrderItem.description: Represents a specific product included in a placed order, capturing its state at the time of purchase.

id.description: Unique identifier for the OrderItem entity.

orderId.description: Reference to the Order this item belongs to. (Relationship: Order 1:N OrderItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product purchased. (Relationship: Product 1:N OrderItem)

productName.description: A snapshot of the product name at the time the order was placed.

quantity.description: The quantity of this product in the order.

priceAtOrder.description: The price of a single unit of the product at the moment of order placement.

selectedConfigurationDetails.description: A snapshot of the selected configuration options and their values, including price adjustments, at the time of order.

CustomServiceRequest.title: CustomServiceRequest
CustomServiceRequest.description: Represents a user's request for custom hardware services like PCB design or product customization.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CustomServiceRequest entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who submitted the request. (Relationship: User 1:N CustomServiceRequest)

requestDate.description: Timestamp when the service request was submitted.

projectDescription.description: A detailed description of the custom project or service required.

fileUrls.description: An array of URLs to files uploaded by the user to support their request (e.g., schematics, design ideas).

budget.description: The user's optional proposed budget for the project.

deadline.description: The user's optional requested deadline for project completion.

serviceType.description: The type of custom service requested (e.g., 'PCB Design', 'Schematic Design', 'Product Customization', 'Enclosure Design').

status.description: The current status of the custom service request (e.g., 'New', 'Under Review', 'Quoted', 'Accepted', 'Rejected', 'Completed').

quoteAmount.description: The quoted monetary amount for the service, provided by an admin (optional).

quoteDetails.description: Detailed description of the quote provided by the admin (optional).

definition.description: Top-level collection for all product categories. This data is public and read-only for all users, primarily used for product catalog navigation. Adheres to structural segregation for homogeneous security posture (public read).

params.name: categoryId
params.description: Unique identifier for the category document.

definition.description: Top-level collection for all products available in the store. This data is public and read-only for all users. Supports QAPs for listing products without user-specific filters, aligning with structural segregation.

params.name: productId
params.description: Unique identifier for the product document.

definition.description: Top-level collection for all product configuration options. These options are public and read-only, linking to products. Enables efficient querying and structural segregation for public data.

params.name: optionId
params.description: Unique identifier for the product configuration option document.

definition.description: Top-level collection for all specific configuration values associated with options. This data is public and read-only, used to define product customizations. Aligns with structural segregation for public data.

params.name: valueId
params.description: Unique identifier for the product configuration value document.

definition.description: Top-level collection storing user profiles. Access is restricted to the authenticated user whose UID matches '{userId}'. This structure enforces private data access via path-based ownership, ensuring Authorization Independence without 'get()' calls.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Subcollection under a user's profile for storing their physical addresses. Access is restricted to the owner user (whose UID matches the parent '{userId}'). This path-based ownership guarantees Authorization Independence for addresses and simplifies security rules for user-specific lists (QAP).

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching Firebase Authentication UID.

params.name: addressId
params.description: Unique identifier for the address document.

definition.description: Subcollection under a user's profile for storing their wishlist items. Access is restricted to the owner user (whose UID matches the parent '{userId}'). This path-based ownership ensures Authorization Independence and supports QAPs for listing user's wishlist.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching Firebase Authentication UID.

params.name: wishlistItemId
params.description: Unique identifier for the wishlist item document.

definition.description: Document representing a user's single shopping cart. Located as a sub-document directly under the user's profile. Access is restricted to the owner user, providing Authorization Independence through path-based ownership. Its ID will typically be a fixed string like 'current_cart'.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Subcollection under a user's cart for individual items within the cart. Access is restricted to the owner user (whose UID matches the grandparent '{userId}'). The hierarchical path provides Authorization Independence, simplifying rules and supporting QAPs for cart item listings.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching Firebase Authentication UID.

params.name: cartItemId
params.description: Unique identifier for the cart item document.

definition.description: Top-level collection for all customer orders. Each order document includes a 'userId' field (denormalized ownership). This design ensures Authorization Independence for individual users (request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId) and allows admins to list all orders (QAP for admin) without relying on 'get()' calls across user subcollections.

params.name: orderId
params.description: Unique identifier for the order document.

definition.description: Subcollection for items within a specific order. Each order item document MUST include the 'userId' denormalized from its parent 'Order' document. This is CRITICAL for Authorization Independence, enabling direct ownership checks (request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId) without a 'get()' call to the parent order, thereby supporting atomic operations and QAPs.

params.name: orderId
params.description: Unique identifier for the parent order document.

params.name: orderItemId
params.description: Unique identifier for the order item document.

definition.description: Top-level collection for custom hardware service requests. Each request document includes a 'userId' field (denormalized ownership). This ensures Authorization Independence for users submitting requests and allows admins to efficiently list all requests (QAP for admin) without complex rules or 'get()' dependencies.

params.name: customServiceRequestId
params.description: Unique identifier for the custom service request document.

definition.description: Top-level collection for defining administrative roles. The mere existence of a document at this path signifies that the user identified by '{adminId}' (which must match request.auth.uid) possesses admin privileges. This uses the 'Existence over Content' principle for DBAC, making admin role checks simple and independent. Documents are typically empty or contain minimal metadata, but conceptually link to a User.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who is an administrator, matching Firebase Authentication UID.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure for MicroChub is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence, debuggability, and support for QAPs (Queries as Policies), following the mandated design principles.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
This principle is achieved primarily through two strategies:
1.  **Path-Based Ownership:** For truly private user data like `Addresses`, `WishlistItems`, and `CartItems`, entities are nested directly under the `/users/{userId}` path (e.g., `/users/{userId}/addresses/{addressId}`). This means the `{userId}` wildcard in the path directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid`, making authorization checks atomic (`request.auth.uid == userId`) without requiring any `get()` operations. This completely eliminates hierarchical authorization dependencies for these critical user-specific subcollections.
2.  **Denormalization of Ownership Fields:** For collections that need to be accessible by a user *and* administrators, or subcollections whose security depends on a grandparent document, the `userId` (owner) is explicitly denormalized into the document itself. For example, `Order` documents in `/orders/{orderId}` contain a `userId` field. Similarly, `CustomServiceRequest` documents in `/custom_service_requests/{customServiceRequestId}` include a `userId`. Most crucially, `OrderItem` documents, which are subcollections of `Order` (`/orders/{orderId}/order_items/{orderItemId}`), also include the `userId` from their parent order. This denormalization allows rules on `OrderItem` to directly check `resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid` without ever needing to `get()` the parent `Order` document, thus maintaining Authorization Independence even for nested data and enabling atomic writes (e.g., creating an Order and its OrderItems in a single batch).

**Clarity of Intent & Debuggability:**
Collection names and wildcards are semantic and explicit (e.g., `products`, `custom_service_requests`, `{productId}`). Authorization fields are consistently named (`userId`). The structure itself makes the security posture clear: data under `/users/{userId}` is user-specific, global collections like `/products` are public, and `/orders` are shared but secured by denormalized `userId`.

**DBAC (Database Access Control - No Custom Claims):**
Global roles, specifically admin access, are managed via the `/roles_admin/{adminId}` collection. The existence of a document for a user's UID in this collection grants admin privileges. Firebase Security Rules can easily check `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` for efficient and clear role-based authorization.

**QAPs (Queries as Policies):**
1.  **Public Collections:** Collections like `/categories`, `/products`, `/product_configuration_options`, and `/product_configuration_values` are designed for public read access. `list` operations here naturally serve as QAPs, allowing any user to read all public items.
2.  **User-Owned Subcollections:** For paths like `/users/{userId}/addresses` or `/users/{userId}/wishlist_items`, rules will enforce that `request.auth.uid == userId` (from the path wildcard) for both `read` and `list` operations. This ensures that users can only query their own data, and the Firestore engine can optimize these queries as a policy.
3.  **Shared Top-Level Collections with Denormalized `userId`:** For `Orders` and `CustomServiceRequests`, `list` operations for regular users are secured by requiring a query filter like `where('userId', '==', request.auth.uid)`. The security rules will explicitly allow `list` only if this filter is present and matches the authenticated user. Administrators, identified via the `/roles_admin` collection, will be granted `list` access to these top-level collections, enabling them to query all orders or requests without user-specific filters, as required by the admin dashboard.
4.  **`OrderItem` Subcollection:** For `order_items` under `/orders/{orderId}/order_items/{orderItemId}`, `list` operations are implicitly secured by the parent `Order`'s rules and the denormalized `userId` within the `OrderItem` document itself. Users can only list items if they have access to the parent order, which is verified through the denormalized `userId` matching `request.auth.uid`.

**Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):**
Data with different access requirements is separated into distinct collections. For example, public product information is in `/products`, while private user data is under `/users/{userId}/`. This simplifies security rules significantly as each collection (or subcollection) inherently has a consistent security profile.
